stub_check.note: Every repository method issues real SQL against the live connection. No in-memory shadow state, no constant return values, no unfinished markers in production paths.

thin_test_check.note: 20 tests exercise semantics, boundaries, negative behavior, persistence-across-restart, concurrency, corruption, and recovery. Not happy-path-only.
behaviors: migration applies, is monotonic, and is idempotent
migration from N-1 preserves pre-existing rows
exact readback after process restart via a new connection
analytics aggregate persisted rows and isolate subtests
attempt recording is exactly-once under replay
evidence vault dedupes by content hash and refuses mutation
PR merge requires explicit named approval and is not repeatable
approval-without-approver is unrepresentable in the schema
backup digest matches the archive on disk
restore rolls back to snapshot state
corrupted backup is rejected and live data untouched
truncated backup is rejected and live data untouched
concurrent writers lose no updates under WAL + busy timeout
content-pack rollback restores the prior active version
opening a directory as a database fails loudly

evidence_sticker_check.note: Evidence files are real command output with exit codes plus SHA-256 hashes, not assertion files. livefire.log contains an executed end-to-end transcript verified by an independent sqlite3 reader.

test_weakening_check.note: No assertion was deleted, skipped, or loosened to obtain a green run. Two tests were corrected because they were initially wrong (missing learner seed and a free-page byte flip), and both corrections made them strictly stronger.

known_limitations: Backup encryption is reported via the manifest 'encrypted' flag but no encryption is applied in this node; REQ-033 requires encryption to be optional, and a plain integrity-checked backup satisfies the current requirement. Encryption at rest is deferred to EP-006 security work and is recorded here as outstanding rather than silently claimed.
Concurrency is proven at process/thread level against a single SQLite file. Multi-machine or network-filesystem concurrency is out of scope for a local-first desktop application (ADR-003).
